Microverse tick 0 · pairs

Flies that inherit how to learn, not what they learned.

A small world of simulated flies. A hidden rule decides which smells are food and which are poison, and every 3,000 ticks it changes. Watch which lineage works it out again.

    Starting the world.

    01

    What Afterwing is

    An artificial-life research project. The long-term aim is agents that learn from experience, then get better at learning itself, measured honestly at every step.

    The question

    Can a creature improve how it learns, not just what it knows? Most learning systems tune numbers inside a fixed design. Afterwing asks whether simulated flies can revise the design itself, which features they pay attention to and how they decide to change them, and pass that ability to their offspring.

    The world

    The Microverse at the top of this page is a closed 40 × 40 world where flies forage, breed and die continuously. Food smells are 8-bit codes, and a hidden formula says which are nutritious. The formula changes every 3,000 ticks, so nothing a fly memorised stays true for long. Offspring inherit their parent's learning program, never its learned weights.

    How we keep it honest

    Every goal is written down before it is tested. Ideas are tuned on practice seeds, then judged once on fresh worlds nobody has seen, against controls: a fixed program, random rewrites, plain evolution. A result that does not clear its pre-set bar is reported as not shown.

    The ladder we are climbing

    1. L0Lifetime learningA fly gets better at telling food from poison during its own life.Shown
    2. L1Program revisionLineages add and drop the features their learning uses, from their own evidence.Shown
    3. L2Reviser tuningFlies retune the settings of the thing that revises them, from a perfect reading of the current brain-cost price.Shown
    4. L3CompoundingEach level makes the next pay off more, at least 1.5×. Eight designs and screens tried; none cleared the bar.Not shown

    This is bounded self-improvement in a hand-built world, not open-ended intelligence, and the flies are not models of real insects. Richer minds, larger worlds and societies remain the long-term direction, not something this code has shown.

    02

    The hidden rule

    Each food smell is an 8-bit code. The rule multiplies some of those bits together and adds the results; the sign says nutritious or toxic. The flies never see the formula. They have to guess which bit-combinations matter.

        Scope: hand-written rules in a constructed world. The self-improvement shown here is bounded: flies revise which features they use and retune their reviser's settings. It is not open-ended intelligence, and these are not models of real insects. G7c and L2 replicated on new seed banks, and later controls narrowed both: about 60% of the L2 benefit comes from reading the price once at birth, and choosing movement senses from evidence beats choosing them at random but not giving the fly the two useful senses from the start.
